<h4 class=name>Dr. Manjari Mishra - Assistant Executive Scientist</h4>
![](/bio/foto/ManjariSingh.png){.float-left height=210px}
Manjari is a biophysicist, pharmacologist, and infectious disease biologist
specializing in analytical sciences and targeted therapeutics. She earned her
Ph.D. in Membrane Biophysics and Chemical Biology from the Indian Institute of
Technology Bombay, India, where she studied how pathogenic lipids from
Mycobacterium tuberculosis alter host cellular functions through membrane
organization and signaling pathways.

Her research has since expanded into virology, antiviral strategies, and
translational therapeutics, with a focus on understanding host–virus
interactions and developing approaches for future pandemic preparedness. In
addition to her research activities, Manjari serves as a consultant through GLG
advisory engagements, is a member of the Stanford Science Consulting Group, and
serves on the editorial board of Frontiers journals.

Manjari became connected with Instituto Dourados through founders Izabela and
Matt during the Stanford Pandemic Preparedness fellowship network, where she had
the opportunity to learn about their impactful work in public health, indigenous
health equity, and community-centered scientific initiatives. Inspired by their
vision and commitment to social reform, she joined the institute to contribute
her scientific expertise toward advancing global collaborations, strengthening
research accessibility, and supporting initiatives focused on indigenous health,
pandemic preparedness, and equitable healthcare innovation.

Outside of research, she enjoys cooking, traveling, and mentoring young
scientists.
